title: Comparison of acoustically and electrically evoked stapedius reflex thresholds
summary:
Cochlear implants (CI) are electronic prostheses that enable people with severe hearing loss or deafness to hear by electrically stimulating the auditory nerve. To achieve the best possible hearing outcome, the CI must be adjusted to the individual needs of the patient. The adjustment of these technical devices is usually based on the patients’ subjective feedback. The subjective nature of this method leads to considerable variability in the quality of the responses. Determining an optimal CI setting can be especially challenging in non-cooperative patients. Inappropriate CI settings can result in a lack of auditory perception, diminished speech recognition, tissue damage, or auditory fatigue.
In this study, an objective measurement method known as stapedius reflex measurement will be applied to both normal-hearing individuals and CI users. Subsequently, these objective measurements will be compared to subjective loudness perception. The aim of this study is to investigate whether stapedius reflexes can serve as an objective tool to support CI programming.
